title: Connectors & architecture description
literature: Taylor, Medvidovic & Dashofy connector taxonomy (procedure-call, event, data-access, linkage, stream, arbitrator, adaptor, distributor); Mehta et al. 'Towards a Taxonomy of Software Connectors'; ADLs (ACME, xADL, Wright).

members.name: 4+1 View Model
members.what: A fixed viewpoint set — logical, process, development, and physical views, plus scenarios (the +1) that tie them together — for describing a software architecture.

members.name: Adaptor Connector
members.what: A connector that converts between mismatched interaction policies, interfaces, or data formats of components not designed to interoperate - wrappers, transformers, and protocol converters.

members.name: Allocation View
members.what: A view type mapping software elements onto structures in the system's environment — hardware and networks (deployment), file systems (implementation), and teams (work assignment).

members.name: Arbitrator Connector
members.what: A connector that resolves conflicts and redirects control among components with conflicting needs, providing concurrency control (locks, semaphores), scheduling, load balancing, and fault-handling negotiation.

members.name: Architectural Perspective
members.what: A collection of activities, tactics, and guidelines for ensuring that a system exhibits a particular quality property, applied across all of a description's views rather than forming a view of its own.

members.name: Architecture Decision Record
members.what: A short, versioned document capturing one architecturally significant decision together with its context, status, and consequences.

members.name: Architecture Description
members.what: The concrete work product (documents, models, views) used to express the architecture of a system of interest.

members.name: Architecture Description Language
members.what: A formal notation whose first-class constructs are architectural — components, connectors, configurations — used to model and analyze a software architecture.

members.name: Architecture Framework
members.what: An established package of conventions, principles, viewpoints, and practices for architecture description within a specific domain or stakeholder community.

members.name: Architecture View
members.what: A representation of a system's architecture from the perspective of a related set of concerns, composed of one or more architecture models.

members.name: Architecture Viewpoint
members.what: A reusable work product establishing the conventions — model kinds, notations, methods — for constructing, interpreting, and using views that frame a specific set of stakeholder concerns.

members.name: AUTOSAR Virtual Function Bus / RTE
members.what: A communication abstraction in which software components interact through typed ports on a virtual bus, generated per-ECU as the runtime environment (RTE) that maps port communication to intra-ECU calls or network signals.

members.name: Component-and-Connector View
members.what: A view type documenting the system's runtime elements (components) and their interaction pathways (connectors) — pipes-and-filters, client-server, publish-subscribe structures and the like.

members.name: Context Map
members.what: A documented map of the system's bounded contexts and the relationship type at each seam (partnership, customer-supplier, conformist, ACL, ...).

members.name: Data Access Connector
members.what: A connector through which a component reads or writes data maintained by a data store or another component, covering repository access, database queries, and accessor operations, often with translation/conversion.

members.name: Distributor Connector
members.what: A connector that identifies interaction paths and routes communication among components - naming, registration/lookup, and delivery services such as DNS-style naming, routing, and multicast distribution.

members.name: Enterprise Service Bus
members.what: A shared messaging backbone providing routing, transformation, protocol bridging, and orchestration between enterprise applications.

members.name: Event Connector
members.what: A connector that transfers control and data by delivering occurrences (events) from producers to registered observers, with dimensions for cardinality, delivery guarantees, synchronicity, and notification mode.

members.name: Interface Definition Language
members.what: A language-neutral contract describing component interfaces and data types from which stubs, skeletons and serializers are generated.

members.name: Linkage Connector
members.what: A connector that ties system elements together by establishing and enforcing associations - name bindings, imports/exports, and compile- or load-time linking - enabling other connectors to act at runtime.

members.name: Message Channel
members.what: A named logical conduit of the messaging system that senders write messages to and receivers read from.

members.name: Model Kind
members.what: The conventions (notation, modeling template, analytic methods) for one type of architecture model used within a viewpoint, e.g. a state-machine or dataflow model kind.

members.name: Module View
members.what: A view type documenting the system's units of implementation (modules) and their static relations — decomposition, uses, layering, generalization, data-model.

members.name: Procedure Call Connector
members.what: A connector that transfers control and data between components through invocation with parameters and (usually) a return, spanning local calls, method invocations, callbacks, and system calls.

members.name: Rozanski–Woods Viewpoint Catalog
members.what: A catalog of seven viewpoints — context, functional, information, concurrency, development, deployment, operational — for describing information-system architectures.

members.name: Secure Channel
members.what: A connector type in which communication between components crosses an authenticated, encrypted transport so confidentiality and integrity hold over untrusted networks.

members.name: Stakeholder Concern
members.what: An interest in the system relevant to one or more stakeholders, used to scope which viewpoints and views an architecture description must provide.

members.name: Stream Connector
members.what: A connector that transfers sequences of data between autonomous processes, covering pipes, sockets, and other bounded/unbounded, buffered, structured or raw data flows.

members.name: Temporal Firewall
members.what: A unidirectional, time-controlled shared-memory interface between subsystems: the sender deposits temporally accurate state data that the receiver reads at predefined instants, with no control signals crossing the interface in either direct

members.name: Time-Triggered Bus
members.what: A broadcast communication channel whose access is governed by a static TDMA schedule: each node owns pre-assigned slots in a cyclic schedule known to all nodes, so message timing is known a priori.
